data.narrative:
Asterra, a Series A space and aerospace company founded by Lauren Guy, has raised $20M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 5 public tickers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, spanning the space and aerospace sector at seed through Series B stages.

Two methods triangulate valuation. Stage-progression applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $20M raised proxy, implying $40M. Peer-median anchors to three same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables—Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B Series B), Aalyria ($1.3B Series B), and Starcloud ($1.1B Seed)—yielding a $1.3B median with a $1.1B to $2.0B range. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable due to absence of target revenue disclosure, though the sector P/S median stands at 27.4x across the 6 public comps identified.

The two applicable methods produce a wide triangulated range of $34M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $670M. This spread reflects the acute tension between stage-based progression (early-stage discount) and peer multiples (mature capital markets for advanced aerospace). Key uncertainties include Asterra's revenue run rate and unit economics relative to Series B peers, which would narrow the range considerably if disclosed. The peer-median floor of $1.1B–$1.3B likely better reflects market precedent for this sector at this stage, though the $40M stage-based floor provides downside anchoring.
